modules.title: Foundations + Northern Hardwood Anchors
objectives: Apply dendrological vocabulary and the maximum-defensible-rank decision rule.
Identify the northern-hardwood anchor taxa from unfamiliar foliage, bark, reproductive, dormant, and whole-tree evidence where defensible.
State a nearest plausible alternative, visible separator, confidence code, and resolving view.
Retrieve canonical common and scientific names and introductory field silvics for every new taxon.
Separate American beech host identity from clean or normal bark condition.

Identify taxa under disease, insect, age, injury, weather, lichen, browse, and poor-view variation.
Identify American beech across the required bark and foliage-condition sequence while scoring host and condition separately.
Make calibrated winter identifications from twigs, buds, scars, pith, thorns, persistent structures, and site.
Choose genus, group, or insufficient evidence when adversarial material cannot defend species.

Complete cumulative scientific-name retrieval in both directions.
Pass separate foliage, bark, reproductive, dormant, whole-tree/regional, and rapid mixed-evidence batteries.
Synthesize field silvics across site, regeneration, disturbance, succession, condition, and management.
Produce a final numerical grade and a separate species-by-modality mastery and certification report.
